plan.vision: Agentic Problem: Recruiters and job seekers waste time manually parsing/validating 'Who wants to be hired?' HN posts. Atomic Milestones: (1) Define strict schema for expected fields; (2) Build pure-function parser using regex with exhaustive validation; (3) Create CLI that reads from stdin/file and outputs JSON; (4) Write 100% coverage unit tests using real HN post examples; (5) Ensure win32 compatibility via pathlib and no curses. Testing Strategy: All core logic tested via parameterized pytest cases with valid/invalid inputs. CLI tested via subprocess. No mocks used—core accepts str, returns dict.
plan.lessons_learned: Avoids past mistakes by: (1) Core parser is pure function accepting str—zero file I/O or side effects; (2) Uses pre-compiled regex for performance in hot loop; (3) Explicit field validation prevents KeyError; (4) CLI uses context-managed file reading with win32-safe pathlib; (5) Tests use real HN post strings—no mocks—ensuring deterministic validation.
plan.commit_message: Implement HireMeParser: CLI tool to validate and parse HN 'Who wants to be hired?' posts into structured JSON.

files_to_generate.instructions: Empty file to make hireme a Python package.

Define ValidationError as subclass of ValueError. Implement parse_hn_hireme_post(content: str) -> dict. Use pre-compiled regex patterns to extract: Location, Remote, Willing to relocate, Technologies, Résumé/CV, Email. Validate each field: Email must match RFC5322-lite regex; Technologies must be non-empty; all fields required. Return dict with normalized keys (e.g., 'resume_cv'). Raise ValidationError with specific message on any failure. Use only stdlib re, typing.

Implement main(). Use argparse to accept optional --input file path (default: stdin). Read content safely using pathlib.Path if file given, else sys.stdin.read(). Call parse_hn_hireme_post. Print result as JSON to stdout. On ValidationError or file error, print error to stderr and exit(1). Wrap in if __name__ == '__main__': block.

Write pytest functions. Part 1: Test parser directly with parameterized cases: (1) Valid full post; (2) Missing field; (3) Invalid email; (4) Empty technologies; (5) Extra whitespace handling. Assert exact dict output or ValidationError. Part 2: Test CLI via subprocess. Create temp file with valid post. Run 'python -m hireme.cli --input <tempfile>'. Assert stdout is valid JSON matching expected dict. Repeat with invalid post—assert stderr contains error and exit code 1. Use pathlib for temp file cleanup. Do NOT mock anything.
Empty file—only stdlib used. But include comment: '# No dependencies required'

Explain: Parses HN 'Who wants to be hired?' posts. Usage: echo '<post>' | python -m hireme.cli or python -m hireme.cli --input post.txt. Output: JSON. Architecture: Pure parser in parser.py, CLI in cli.py. Testing: Full coverage with real examples. Win32 safe. No deps.
